issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the provided template Stock class defines a method named clearInventory(). This name/signature mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may cause tests or instructor-provided code (which expect emptyStock) to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement/UML and solution to use clearInventory(). Preferably, align the template to the UML by adding/renaming the method to public void emptyStock() to match the specification and solution.

issues.description: The Stock method used to clear all inventory is named inconsistently across artifacts: the Problem Statement (UML) and the Solution implement emptyStock(), whereas the Template repository's Stock class provides clearInventory(). This mismatch means students reading the template will not find the emptyStock() method referenced in the specification and solution, creating confusion about which method to use or implement and increasing friction when mapping requirements to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add an emptyStock() wrapper that delegates to clearInventory(), and update any references so the Problem Statement, template, and solution use the same identifier emptyStock().
